_comment: Models the Private Assistant offers. download_bytes = sum of the layers in the Ollama library manifest (checked 2026-11-04 on registry.ollama.ai); the page uses it until Ollama reports the real total. min_ram_gib = smallest box (memory as Linux reports it, in GiB: a 32 GB box shows about 30, 64 GB about 62, 96 GB about 93, 128 GB about 123) that may use the model next to an Ethereum node, which needs about 20-25 GB itself. recommend_from_gib = from which box size it is the automatic choice (null: only on request). think = what the speed test sends as Ollama's think value (gpt-oss always thinks and takes a level).

models.name: Qwen3 1.7B
models.label: Very small
models.about: Light and quick. Fine for short questions and simple writing help, but it makes more mistakes than the bigger models.

models.name: Qwen3 4B
models.label: Small
models.about: Small and quick. Good for everyday questions, short summaries and writing help.

models.name: gpt-oss 20B
models.label: Medium, thinks first
models.about: OpenAI's open model. It thinks before it answers, so the first words take longer, but it is better at step-by-step problems.

models.name: Qwen3 30B
models.label: Medium
models.about: Much smarter than the small models and still quick, because it only uses a small part of itself for each word.

models.name: Qwen3-Next 80B
models.label: Big
models.about: Knows a lot more than the medium models and is about as quick, because it also uses only a small part of itself for each word. For boxes with 96 GB of memory or more.

models.name: gpt-oss 120B
models.label: Large
models.about: The smartest choice, for boxes with 128 GB of memory. It thinks before it answers and is slower than the medium models.
